items.title: 'I wish he was rescued quickly': Mourning families speak after PG collapse
items.summary: “His birthday is in October, he would’ve turned 20,” said Pushpa, recalling her son Arpit Jahaj's last birthday, when the family surprised him with a silver bracelet. “His bracelet and neck chain were gone. I was able to identify my son only with the birthmark near his shoulder,” she said. Arpit, a second-year student at Delhi University’s Atma Ram Sanatan Dharm College, had returned to Delhi from his home in Madhya Pradesh on the morning of Sunday, September 6, after spending Rakshabandhan with his family. By Monday afternoon, after the debris was cleared at the Satya Niketan collapse site, he was among the seven confirmed dead. Five others who were injured are receiving treatment. He had last spoken to his mother around 12:30 pm on Sunday. The family rushed to Delhi from their home in Dewas, Madhya Pradesh, after being informed of the incident by Arpit’s uncle who lives in Ghaziabad. At the AIIMS Trauma Centre, the waiting room was a daunting place. “We had to wait for a long time to see our son. The police made us wait,” said Pushpa.
